answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused to reopen pricing while finance mandates 18% cost reduction. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing—exactly what the current constraint requires. Verifying memory_c2 confirms the feasibility and speed of vendor transition. The 14-day contract expiration window is tight but memory_c2 suggests this vendor can onboard quickly. However, at 94% committed volume with no buffer, switching primary supply introduces delivery risk if the new vendor stumbles; this risk is flagged. memory_c4 shows negotiation worked before but the incumbent has already refused. memory_c6 shows multi-year terms unlock pricing, but we lack time to negotiate that now. Switching primary vendor is the only lever that addresses both the 18% mandate and the binding contract deadline. A standard experiment scale allows rapid validation before full commitment, mitigating some execution risk while the assembly line operates near capacity.
